title: Add download_amazon_invoice tool + two fixes for get_amazon_orders
body:
Hi Marcus, thanks for the MCP — I've been using it as the backbone of a small accounting workflow.

While building that I ended up with three things I thought might be worth contributing back: a new `download_amazon_invoice` tool I needed for capturing invoice PDFs, and two small fixes in `get_amazon_orders` that I came across along the way. They're separate commits so you can take any subset you'd like.

**The new tool** — `download_amazon_invoice` saves an order's invoice as a PDF, so it can be archived or attached to a bookkeeping record. It navigates to the same `/gp/css/summary/print.html` URL that `extractFromInvoice()` already uses, waits for the page to settle, and renders A4 with `page.pdf()`. Returns a structured error rather than saving the wrong page if the session has expired or the order isn't accessible.

**Qty attribution fix** — On multi-item shipments where one item has `qty > 1`, the qty badge was being attributed to the wrong item. `extractItemsFromDataComponents` was reading title / price / qty elements as flat lists scoped to the whole `purchasedItems` container and pairing them by index — but Amazon only renders the `.od-item-view-qty` badge when `qty > 1`, so the lists don't actually align. The fix scopes each item's lookups to its own `.a-fixed-left-grid` row (which Amazon already uses to group each item's image and details). Comes with a small hand-crafted HTML fixture and a new test that walks the affected shape.

**Date filter fix** — `start_date` / `end_date` were being silently dropped, so a 7-day query would return the whole year. Two pieces: `getOrderListUrl` now picks the narrowest `timeFilter` that covers the requested range (Amazon's URL doesn't accept custom date ranges, so it's the best we can do at that level), and `fetchOrders` trims each page to the actual window and then stops paginating once it walks past `start_date`. Brings a 7-day live query down from ~35s to ~5s.

**Verification** — typecheck is clean, 63 unit + 2 integration tests passing, and the date filter change was tested end-to-end against a live UK account.

If any of this isn't quite the right shape for the project, happy to split, rework, or drop bits — just let me know.

---

This PR was drafted with Claude Opus 4.7 — I reviewed and tested each commit before pushing.

title: Allow BROWSER_DATA_DIR override via env var
fix: handle redesigned transactions page + cross-year order ranges
body:
## What

Two fixes for breakage observed on amazon.com.au (July 2026), likely affecting other regions as Amazon rolls out the redesigned payments UI:

**1. `get_amazon_transactions` returned one garbage row.** Amazon replaced the infinite-scroll transactions page with a paginated layout using `apx-*` class names (`.apx-transaction-date-container`, `.apx-transactions-line-item-component-container`). None of the existing selectors matched, so the generic `.a-row` fallback scraped the whole page into a single "transaction" with vendor `"There was a problem"` and every order ID lumped together. This PR adds an apx-structure extraction strategy (tried first, legacy strategies kept as fallbacks) and paginates via the `DefaultNextPageNavigationEvent` submit button, with scrolling retained for legacy layouts. Rows scraped off Amazon error banners are filtered out.

**2. Cross-year date ranges silently missed orders.** Amazon's order-history URL only supports `year-YYYY` / `months-N` filters, so a start/end range spanning years only fetched the first year. Ranges are now split into per-year requests and merged.

Also included:
- Bare `$` amounts were always parsed as USD; the transactions page now trusts the region's currency (e.g. AUD on amazon.com.au).
- The server relaunches its persistent browser if it dies (crash, window closed, killed) instead of failing every subsequent tool call with "browser has been closed".

## Testing

Verified against a live amazon.com.au account, driving the built server over MCP stdio JSON-RPC:
- `get_amazon_transactions` (6-month range): 68 transactions across 4 pages, each with its own order ID, correct AUD amounts, card info, vendor, and status.
- `get_amazon_orders` with `include_items` across a year boundary: orders and item details extracted correctly.

title: GH#14: fix row-scoped modern item extraction
body:
## Summary

- bind modern Amazon item fields within each `.a-fixed-left-grid` row
- reuse that extractor for invoice, bulk/detail, and single-order paths
- preserve singleton containers that have no row wrapper while skipping ambiguous multi-title containers
